title: Job, Chapter 15 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Job 15 on folios 401r, 401v of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Job chapter 15 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 401r, 401v.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ <sup>2</sup>הֶֽחָכָ֗ם יַעֲנֶ֥ה דַֽעַת־ר֑וּחַ וִֽימַלֵּ֖א קָדִ֣ים בִּטְנֽוֹ׃ <sup>3</sup>הוֹכֵ֣חַ בְּ֭דָבָר לֹ֣א יִסְכּ֑וֹן וּ֝מִלִּ֗ים לֹא־יוֹעִ֥יל בָּֽם׃ <sup>4</sup>אַף־אַ֭תָּה תָּפֵ֣ר יִרְאָ֑ה וְתִגְרַ֥ע שִׂ֝יחָ֗ה לִפְנֵי־אֵֽל׃ <sup>5</sup>כִּ֤י יְאַלֵּ֣ף עֲוֺנְךָ֣ פִ֑יךָ וְ֝תִבְחַ֗ר לְשׁ֣וֹן עֲרוּמִֽים׃ <sup>6</sup>יַרְשִֽׁיעֲךָ֣ פִ֣יךָ וְלֹא־אָ֑נִי וּ֝שְׂפָתֶ֗יךָ יַעֲנוּ־בָֽךְ׃ <sup>7</sup>הֲרִאישׁ֣וֹן אָ֭דָם תִּוָּלֵ֑ד וְלִפְנֵ֖י גְבָע֣וֹת חוֹלָֽלְתָּ׃ <sup>8</sup>הַבְס֣וֹד אֱל֣וֹהַ תִּשְׁמָ֑ע וְתִגְרַ֖ע אֵלֶ֣יךָ חָכְמָֽה׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said, <sup>2</sup>Should a wise man utter vain knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind? <sup>3</sup>Should he reason with unprofitable talk? or with speeches wherewith he can do no good? <sup>4</sup>Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God. <sup>5</sup>For thy mouth uttereth thine iniquity, and thou choosest the tongue of the crafty. <sup>6</sup>Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I: yea, thine own lips testify against thee. <sup>7</sup>Art thou the first man that was born? or wast thou made before the hills? <sup>8</sup>Hast thou heard the secret of God? and dost thou restrain wisdom to thyself?

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>מַה־יָּ֭דַעְתָּ וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע תָּ֝בִ֗ין וְֽלֹא־עִמָּ֥נוּ הֽוּא׃ <sup>10</sup>גַּם־שָׂ֣ב גַּם־יָשִׁ֣ישׁ בָּ֑נוּ כַּבִּ֖יר מֵאָבִ֣יךָ יָמִֽים׃ <sup>11</sup>הַמְעַ֣ט מִ֭מְּךָ תַּנְחֻמ֣וֹת אֵ֑ל וְ֝דָבָ֗ר לָאַ֥ט עִמָּֽךְ׃ <sup>12</sup>מַה־יִּקָּחֲךָ֥ לִבֶּ֑ךָ וּֽמַה־יִּרְזְמ֥וּן עֵינֶֽיךָ׃ <sup>13</sup>כִּֽי־תָשִׁ֣יב אֶל־אֵ֣ל רוּחֶ֑ךָ וְהֹצֵ֖אתָ מִפִּ֣יךָ מִלִּֽין׃ <sup>14</sup>מָֽה־אֱנ֥וֹשׁ כִּֽי־יִזְכֶּ֑ה וְכִֽי־יִ֝צְדַּ֗ק יְל֣וּד אִשָּֽׁה׃ <sup>15</sup>הֵ֣ן בקדשו [בִּ֭קְדֹשָׁיו] לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֑ין וְ֝שָׁמַ֗יִם לֹא־זַכּ֥וּ בְעֵינָֽיו׃ <sup>16</sup>אַ֭ף כִּֽי־נִתְעָ֥ב וְֽנֶאֱלָ֑ח אִישׁ־שֹׁתֶ֖ה כַמַּ֣יִם עַוְלָֽה׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>What knowest thou, that we know not? what understandest thou, which is not in us? <sup>10</sup>With us are both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father. <sup>11</sup>Are the consolations of God small with thee? is there any secret thing with thee? <sup>12</sup>Why doth thine heart carry thee away? and what do thy eyes wink at, <sup>13</sup>That thou turnest thy spirit against God, and lettest such words go out of thy mouth? <sup>14</sup>What is man, that he should be clean? and he which is born of a woman, that he should be righteous? <sup>15</sup>Behold, he putteth no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight. <sup>16</sup>How much more abominable and filthy is man, which drinketh iniquity like water?

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>אֲחַוְךָ֥ שְֽׁמַֽע־לִ֑י וְזֶֽה־חָ֝זִ֗יתִי וַאֲסַפֵּֽרָה׃ <sup>18</sup>אֲשֶׁר־חֲכָמִ֥ים יַגִּ֑ידוּ וְלֹ֥א כִֽ֝חֲד֗וּ מֵאֲבוֹתָֽם׃ <sup>19</sup>לָהֶ֣ם לְ֭בַדָּם נִתְּנָ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ וְלֹא־עָ֖בַר זָ֣ר בְּתוֹכָֽם׃ <sup>20</sup>כָּל־יְמֵ֣י רָ֭שָׁע ה֣וּא מִתְחוֹלֵ֑ל וּמִסְפַּ֥ר שָׁ֝נִ֗ים נִצְפְּנ֥וּ לֶעָרִֽיץ׃ <sup>21</sup>קוֹל־פְּחָדִ֥ים בְּאָזְנָ֑יו בַּ֝שָּׁל֗וֹם שׁוֹדֵ֥ד יְבוֹאֶֽנּוּ׃ <sup>22</sup>לֹא־יַאֲמִ֣ין שׁ֭וּב מִנִּי־חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וצפו [וְצָפ֖וּי] ה֣וּא אֱלֵי־חָֽרֶב׃ <sup>23</sup>נֹ֘דֵ֤ד ה֣וּא לַלֶּ֣חֶם אַיֵּ֑ה יָדַ֓ע ׀ כִּֽי־נָכ֖וֹן בְּיָד֣וֹ יֽוֹם־חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃ <sup>24</sup>יְֽ֭בַעֲתֻהוּ צַ֣ר וּמְצוּקָ֑ה תִּ֝תְקְפֵ֗הוּ כְּמֶ֤לֶךְ ׀ עָתִ֬יד לַכִּידֽוֹר׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>I will shew thee, hear me; and that which I have seen I will declare; <sup>18</sup>Which wise men have told from their fathers, and have not hid it: <sup>19</sup>Unto whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger passed among them. <sup>20</sup>The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden to the oppressor. <sup>21</sup>A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. <sup>22</sup>He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword. <sup>23</sup>He wandereth abroad for bread, saying, Where is it? he knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand. <sup>24</sup>Trouble and anguish shall make him afraid; they shall prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>כִּֽי־נָטָ֣ה אֶל־אֵ֣ל יָד֑וֹ וְאֶל־שַׁ֝דַּ֗י יִתְגַּבָּֽר׃ <sup>26</sup>יָר֣וּץ אֵלָ֣יו בְּצַוָּ֑אר בַּ֝עֲבִ֗י גַּבֵּ֥י מָֽגִנָּֽיו׃ <sup>27</sup>כִּֽי־כִסָּ֣ה פָנָ֣יו בְּחֶלְבּ֑וֹ וַיַּ֖עַשׂ פִּימָ֣ה עֲלֵי־כָֽסֶל׃ <sup>28</sup>וַיִּשְׁכּ֤וֹן ׀ עָ֘רִ֤ים נִכְחָד֗וֹת בָּ֭תִּים לֹא־יֵ֣שְׁבוּ לָ֑מוֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר הִתְעַתְּד֣וּ לְגַלִּֽים׃ <sup>29</sup>לֹֽא־יֶ֭עְשַׁר וְלֹא־יָק֣וּם חֵיל֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־יִטֶּ֖ה לָאָ֣רֶץ מִנְלָֽם׃ <sup>30</sup>לֹֽא־יָס֨וּר ׀ מִנִּי־חֹ֗שֶׁךְ יֹֽ֭נַקְתּוֹ תְּיַבֵּ֣שׁ שַׁלְהָ֑בֶת וְ֝יָס֗וּר בְּר֣וּחַ פִּֽיו׃ <sup>31</sup>אַל־יַאֲמֵ֣ן בשו [בַּשָּׁ֣יו] נִתְעָ֑ה כִּי־שָׁ֝֗וְא תִּהְיֶ֥ה תְמוּרָתֽוֹ׃ <sup>32</sup>בְּֽלֹא־י֭וֹמוֹ תִּמָּלֵ֑א וְ֝כִפָּת֗וֹ לֹ֣א רַעֲנָֽנָה׃
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>For he stretcheth out his hand against God, and strengtheneth himself against the Almighty. <sup>26</sup>He runneth upon him, even on his neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers: <sup>27</sup>Because he covereth his face with his fatness, and maketh collops of fat on his flanks. <sup>28</sup>And he dwelleth in desolate cities, and in houses which no man inhabiteth, which are ready to become heaps. <sup>29</sup>He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he prolong the perfection thereof upon the earth. <sup>30</sup>He shall not depart out of darkness; the flame shall dry up his branches, and by the breath of his mouth shall he go away. <sup>31</sup>Let not him that is deceived trust in vanity: for vanity shall be his recompence. <sup>32</sup>It shall be accomplished before his time, and his branch shall not be green.

translation.original_text: <sup>33</sup>יַחְמֹ֣ס כַּגֶּ֣פֶן בִּסְר֑וֹ וְיַשְׁלֵ֥ךְ כַּ֝זַּ֗יִת נִצָּתֽוֹ׃ <sup>34</sup>כִּֽי־עֲדַ֣ת חָנֵ֣ף גַּלְמ֑וּד וְ֝אֵ֗שׁ אָכְלָ֥ה אָֽהֳלֵי־שֹֽׁ֥חַד׃ <sup>35</sup>הָרֹ֣ה עָ֭מָל וְיָלֹד אָ֑וֶן וּ֝בִטְנָ֗ם תָּכִ֥ין מִרְמָֽה׃ ס
translation.text: <sup>33</sup>He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive. <sup>34</sup>For the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery. <sup>35</sup>They conceive mischief, and bring forth vanity, and their belly prepareth deceit.
